key_insight: This paper argues that agent world models should not try to predict every future observation or tool output. Instead, they should focus on editing the agent’s internal task state so it stays accurate, grounded, and free of outdated assumptions.
problem_solved: It addresses two key issues in LLM agents: reconstructing high-entropy, execution-dependent tool responses is often unhelpful when real feedback already exists, and "task-state contamination" causes stale plans, false assumptions, and irrelevant history to accumulate during long-horizon tasks.
method: Represent the world model as an editor of the agent’s internal state rather than a simulator of all environment observations.
Continuously update task state by removing unsupported assumptions and obsolete plans while preserving useful execution context.
Use real tool feedback and environment signals to keep the agent aligned with the current task instead of relying on speculative prediction.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this reframes world modeling for agents around state maintenance and correction, which can improve long-horizon reliability and planning quality. It may also reduce wasted compute on low-value prediction and make agent behavior more robust in dynamic environments.

paper_title: Agent-Editing World Model: Rethinking World Modeling for LLM Agents
paper_authors: Shuang Sun, Guoxin Chen, Fanzhe Meng, Jia Deng, Huatong Song
